title: Face-Derived Evidence Provenance - live demonstration
purpose: A step-by-step walkthrough of the pipeline running end to end: a derived face image is searched on the live web, candidates are verified with face embeddings, the evidence is canonicalised and its hash is recorded on Base Sepolia, and the record is then checked independently, tampered with, tested against the wrong person, and re-submitted.

conventions.shell: Windows PowerShell. Every command is run from the task3 directory.
conventions.terminal_A: PowerShell in task3, using the project environment (.venv). Runs the pipeline and the demonstration scripts.
conventions.terminal_B: A second PowerShell in task3, with the web3-only environment (fresh) activated. Contains web3 and the Python standard library only - none of the face, vision or search libraries the pipeline uses. Used for independent verification.
conventions.browser: Base Sepolia block explorer, open on the registry contract: https://sepolia.basescan.org/address/0x38157D4652304BA251edCcffa435A0bC3F55305a#code

placeholders.CHAIN_TX: The chain transaction hash printed in the same summary panel at the end of step 2.

conventions.input_image: data\input_pichai_run2.jpg - a re-encoded crop of a Wikimedia Commons photograph of a public figure. Live search results change over time; this walkthrough uses this input.

steps.title: The input is a derived artifact
steps.demonstrates: The query image is created locally by cropping, rescaling and re-encoding a source photograph, so its exact bytes have never been published. An exact-file or reverse-hash lookup therefore cannot explain any match found later; a match has to come from the face.

commands.purpose: Derives the query image from the source fixture and prints a byte-level comparison of the two files.

steps.title: Live search, face verification, ranking and chain write
steps.demonstrates: One command runs the whole pipeline against the live web: face detection and embedding, a live Google Lens query, candidate download, per-candidate face verification, evidence ranking, canonicalisation, hashing, and the on-chain record. The run takes roughly a minute; narrate over the output as it appears.

commands.purpose: Runs the full pipeline on the derived input and writes a complete audit trail to runs\RUN_ID.

show: [FACE] lines: RetinaFace detection confidence, face size in pixels, the sharpness gate, the model name (InsightFace buffalo_l, ArcFace w600k_r50, 512-dimension embedding, cosine on L2-normalised vectors), and the six test-time augmentation views.
[SEARCH] lines: the query image uploaded directly to the search provider (never to a public host) and the number of candidates returned by the live Google Lens query.
[FETCH] lines: each candidate image downloaded with its content type, size and SHA-256.
[VERIFY] lines: for each candidate, the cosine similarity with its range across the augmented views, the face-region perceptual hash distance, and the per-candidate verdict.

The ranked table. Explain the ordering: candidates are ranked by verdict tier first (distinct photograph above same-photograph republication), then evidence strength, then cosine. A republication of the same photograph can score a higher cosine than a genuinely different photograph and is still ranked below it, because near-identical pixels show that a file was copied rather than that a face was recognised.

The DISTINCT-ARTIFACT PROOF panel: the input and matched SHA-256 values, whether the files are identical, the cosine interval, the calibrated threshold with its operating point, the face-region pHash distance against the same-photo cutoff, the verdict, and the evidence strength.
The [EVIDENCE] line with the SHA-256 of the canonical evidence object.
The [CHAIN] lines: network, block, gas and cost of the registry write.
The JUDGE SUMMARY panel.

steps.title: The record on chain
steps.demonstrates: The evidence hash from step 2 is held by a public, source-verified contract. The contract stores the hash, a salted subject commitment, the source domain and a first-seen timestamp - never an image, an embedding or a full URL.

Show the transaction's input data, which carries the evidence hash.
Return to the contract page, Contract tab, and show the verified source code, including recordEvidence and getEvidence.

steps.title: Independent verification without the pipeline
steps.demonstrates: The evidence can be checked by someone who does not trust, or even install, the pipeline. verify.py imports only web3 and the standard library, re-implements canonicalisation instead of importing it, recomputes the hash from the bundle, and reads the registry directly.

steps.title: Tamper detection
steps.demonstrates: Any change to the notarised claim is detected. The notarised claim is the evidence object inside the bundle; its canonical SHA-256 is what the registry holds. Bundle context outside that object - notes, runner_up_scores, chain and run_id - is deliberately not part of the hash, so the record can be annotated later without appearing tampered, and the verifier never relies on those fields: it locates the on-chain record by hashing the evidence object itself.

commands.run: Remove-Item -Recurse -Force tampered -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Copy-Item -Recurse sample_run_2 tampered

steps.title: The wrong person
steps.demonstrates: The calibrated threshold rejects a different person. A probe image of a different public figure is scored against the same candidate set as step 2, with the same embedding pipeline and the same threshold, alongside the run's own input for comparison. Uses only images already on disk: no network, no search quota and no gas.

steps.title: First-seen semantics
steps.demonstrates: The registry records the first sighting of a piece of evidence. Re-submitting a hash that is already recorded is refused by the contract, so a record cannot be overwritten, re-dated, or claimed later by someone else.

commands.purpose: Reads the existing on-chain record for the evidence hash from step 2 and attempts to record the same hash again.

steps.title: What this does and does not establish
points: The chain notarises when a claim was made and that it has not changed since. It does not attest that the claim is correct.
A cosine above the threshold identifies a same-subject candidate. It is not a confirmed identity.
No biometric data is written to the chain: the registry holds a salted commitment, with a per-record salt kept off-chain.
Performance across demographic groups has not been measured; the attempts and why they were discarded are documented in ETHICS.md.
Demonstration subjects are public figures only.

fallback.when: The live search in step 2 cannot run - no network, or the search provider is unavailable - or its candidates cannot be verified.
fallback.requires: The captured run runs\20260904T163955Z_c56949 on the demonstration machine. It is the run committed as sample_run_2 and uses the same input image.

commands.purpose: Replays step 2 from the captured provider responses and candidate images, with no network calls. A banner states that it is a replay. The replay writes to a new run directory, leaves the captured run unchanged, and writes nothing to the chain.

then: Say that the output is a replay; the banner remains on screen.
A replay re-stamps the evidence with a new retrieval time, so its evidence hash is not the notarised one.
For steps 3 to 7, use the original run instead of the replay: RUN_ID = 20260904T163955Z_c56949 and CHAIN_TX = 0xe3b94010676d6881429d40139fd667f11de4ba987d565da200d16c52602ca754.
